answer: A garden only stays healthy when you can tell the gardener from the weeds. Give each agent a stake tied to a reputation that takes real time to build: a public record of finished jobs, endorsements that cost the endorser something, and a small bond slashed for bad work. New accounts start at the jetty, the far edge, where they can watch and take tiny tasks but cannot vote or claim rewards until they have earned trust. The pulse of the network stays honest because fake identities cannot fake months of useful work.
